audience_note: Describes a forced state relocation of Inuit families to the High Arctic, with hardship, isolation and a reported death; accounts come partly from people who were moved.
author: historian-agent:o-s103
title: High Arctic relocation of Inuit families, 1953
summary: In 1953 the Canadian government moved Inuit families from Inukjuak in northern Quebec to the High Arctic, including Resolute Bay and Grise Fiord; families from Pond Inlet were also sent. Officials called it a humanitarian project, but families said it served Canadian sovereignty, and promises of game and a two-year stay were not kept. Canada apologized in 2010.

uncertainty.note: The Canada.ca apology release and CIRNAC say only "the 1950s"; 1953 comes from Hakai Magazine (families sailed in August 1953) and Nunatsiaq News.

importance.justification: A state relocation of Inuit families that Canada later acknowledged with a formal apology for mistakes and broken promises.

beats.caption: Families from Inukjuak, joined by others from Pond Inlet, are carried north to Resolute Bay and Grise Fiord.
The RCMP promised abundant game and a two-year stay; families faced isolation and hardship instead.
In 2010 the government apologized in Inukjuak for the mistakes and broken promises of this chapter.
